prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which heterobifunctional small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to a chosen protein and induce its destruction by the proteasome

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation (B029) remains my preferred single part. As a synthetic chemist I find the invention content decisive: a designed heterobifunctional molecule, with tunable linker, ligase ligand and ternary-complex cooperativity, converts pharmacology from occupancy-driven inhibition into catalytic, event-driven removal of a target. The founding demonstration (Sakamoto, Crews and Deshaies, 2001) was followed by cell-permeable degraders and, through Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures, by rules that make design rational rather than empirical. Independent laboratories have confirmed the mechanism for over two decades, and the first-round exchange shows that this is the one candidate that holds up under every member's criteria. My configuration is unchanged from round 1: Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with a citation confined to heterobifunctional degraders.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, so clinical vindication is incomplete. My configuration omits Handa and Ito (cereblon, hence the glue strand), Sakamoto (co-author of the 2001 paper), Gray and Kim, and a narrow citation can look like an arbitrary cut. If the committee judges that a prize must cover the cereblon strand, my citation fails that test. B043 remains the more mature and cleanly attributed alternative, but a second Pd cross-coupling prize after 2010 is a real objection.

responses.point: Linke moved from Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli to Crews, Deshaies and Handa because a prize naming only the heterobifunctional strand would read as incomplete.
responses.response: I take the completeness argument seriously, but it is not decisive for me. Linke himself notes that the PROTAC and glue lineages were discovered separately. A citation that joins them states a unity that the history does not support, and a three-name cap forces that blur. Handa and Ito identified a target for an old drug; Crews and Deshaies conceived a designed modality. The glue strand and Handa deserve recognition, but under the cap I would rather the citation be accurate about what it covers than broad. I therefore keep Ciulli, whose VHL ligands made PROTACs drug-like, and I have not moved.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Handa in the configuration so that the prize is about the principle and not one compound class, and notes that three opening ballots chose Ciulli over Handa or over Deshaies.
responses.response: The principle of induced proximity is common to PROTACs and glues, I agree, but a prize is credited to discoveries. Cereblon showed how thalidomide works; it did not itself provide a design method. Aqvist's own remark that the strands arose separately argues for a narrow citation. I accept his point that choosing Ciulli over Handa is a judgment on discovery type, not on prominence, and I make it on that basis: the VHL ligand and ternary-complex structures supplied the design rules, and Ciulli is the only one of the candidate third names whose work stands inside the heterobifunctional line. If the committee prefers Handa, I could vote for that configuration over losing B029.

responses.point: Brzezinski concedes that B029 is the configuration that survives discussion and that credit is contested, with Ciulli a live contender and the stable fallback being the older B056.
responses.response: I agree that his honesty about overweighting his own field is the right standard. On the chair's maturity question, I do not think B056 is a safer choice: it has no support beyond one ballot and a narrower reach. Absence of an approved degrader is a caution for me but not a reason to defer; the mechanism is validated in many groups, and I would treat sufficient evidence as already present. I also note that his alternatives treat Ciulli as a contender over Deshaies, but I would not drop Deshaies, since the 2001 paper is the founding proof of principle.

responses.point: Sparr proposes a two-part prize, B055 (Hyman, Brangwynne) plus B006 (Cullis alone), arguing from physical-chemical substance and not from the opening tally.
responses.response: I respect that she argues from substance and states the tally does not support her pair. For the chair's question on a two-part prize, I cannot justify a second part independently of B029. B055 is contested as to which cellular assemblies are true liquids, and B006 requires dropping Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Langer and Anderson, with the 2023 Medicine prize overlapping the application. These are real arguments from her own case_against, and they keep me with a single part.

responses.point: Zou narrows base editing (B047) to Liu alone, noting the 2020 CRISPR overlap and the Kondo and Nishida question.
responses.response: The narrowing to Liu alone makes the attribution clean, but it does not answer the overlap with the 2020 prize, and it loses Komor and Gaudelli, who did the decisive bench work. I find B047 a distinct chemical invention, protein chemistry acting on DNA, and I now list it as an alternative because it is the second most plausible part in the opening tally, but its clinical record is younger and I see no reason to place it alongside B029.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a B029 citation restricted to heterobifunctional degraders that omits cereblon, Handa, Ito and Sakamoto.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes B029 premature; I do not think so, but I cannot rule out that others will weigh it more heavily.
For B043, whether a second Pd cross-coupling prize after 2010 is acceptable, and how the Kosugi and Migita precedent affects attribution; my recollection of the early history is from memory.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I know of no specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr and trained under Masamune, but none of the shortlisted candidates is a colleague, student or collaborator documented in my profile.
